learning_objective: 🎯 Step into the shoes of a manufacturer! Learn how firms combine inputs to produce output, and analyze the different types of costs they face.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The technological relationship between physical inputs (like labor and machinery) and physical output. Q = f(L, K) where Q is output, L is labor, and K is capital.
In the short run, at least one factor of production is fixed (like a factory building). In the long run, all factors are variable (you can build new factories).

In the short run, as you add more and more variable inputs (labor) to a fixed input (land), the marginal product initially increases, then decreases, and eventually becomes negative. (Too many cooks spoil the broth!).
Fixed Costs (TFC) don't change with output (like rent). Variable Costs (TVC) change directly with output (like raw materials). Total Cost = TFC + TVC.

fun_activity.title: 🍔 The Burger Kitchen
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine a tiny burger kitchen (Fixed Capital). One chef cooks 10 burgers. Add a 2nd chef, they cooperate, output jumps to 25 (Increasing Returns). Add a 10th chef in the same tiny kitchen—they bump into each other, drop ingredients, and total output falls! This is Negative Marginal Product.

exam_tips: 📌 The Marginal Cost (MC) curve is U-shaped due to the Law of Variable Proportions.
📌 The relationship between AC and MC is heavily tested: When MC < AC, AC falls. When MC > AC, AC rises. MC intersects AC exactly at AC's minimum point.
📌 Total Fixed Cost (TFC) is a horizontal line parallel to the X-axis because it remains constant regardless of output level.
quick_recap: ⭐ Average Fixed Cost (AFC) continuously falls as output increases because a fixed amount is being divided by a larger and larger number.
⭐ The three stages of production are: Increasing Returns, Diminishing Returns, and Negative Returns. A rational producer always operates in Stage 2.
⭐ Marginal Cost only depends on Variable Cost, because Fixed Costs do not change when one extra unit is produced.
